sentences.text: Poonam Kumari vs Pranav Kumar on 15 July, 2024

Bench: C.T. Ravikumar, Prashant Kumar Mishra
 1
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Civil Original Jurisdiction
 Transfer Petition(C) No. 1079 Of 2024
 Poonam Kumari Pet
 Versus
 Pranav Kumar Respondent
 O R D E R

1. This petition is filed under Section 25 of the Code of Civil Procedure seeking transfer of Divorce Case No. 10/2024 titled Pranav Kumar vs. Poonam Kumari pending before the Family Court,
Madhepura District, Bihar to the Family Court, Tis Hazari (Central) District, Delhi.

entities.text: Divorce Case No. 10/2024 titled Pranav Kumar vs. Poonam Kumari
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Family Court, Tis Hazari (Central) District, Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Finding an element for settlement from the submissions made across the Bar, by the learned counsel for the parties, the parties were sent for mediation, which was successfully conducted and ultimately culminated in the Settlement Agreement dated 4.6.2024.
The Settlement Agreement is taken on record.
3. Paragraph 3 of the Settlement Agreement would reveal that some cases are pending between the parties.
The terms and conditions of the settlement are set out in paragraph 6 of the agreement.

The major conditions, among others, of the 17:05:43 IST Reason:
settlement read as follows:-
A. It is agreed between the petitioner/wife and respondent/husband that there is no possibility of renunion due to irreconcilable differences and as such, they have decided to part their ways and go for dissolution of their marriage by mutual consent in accordance with law as provided under Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act.
Both the parties further agree to file appropriate application before the Honble Supreme Court of India before the next date of hearing in T.P.(C) No. 1079/2024 pending adjudication before this Honble Court.
xxxxx D.

That the respondent/husband has agreed to pay an amount of Rs.12,50,000/- (Rupees Twelve Lakhs Fifty Thousand only) towards the full and final Poonam Kumari vs Pranav Kumar on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69687557/

entities.text: Poonam Kumari vs Pranav Kumar on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 maintenance (upbringing/education) of the baby boy namely Naman along with the maintenance, permanent alimony and full and final settlement of all the past/present and future claims of the petitioner.
The petitioner underatakes not to put forthy any further claim towards her permanent alimony/maintenance (past, present and future)/full and final settlement in future at any stage.
xxxxx G.

It is agreed between parties that the husband shall pay the above-said settled amount of Ra.12,50,000/- (Rupees Twelve Lakhs Fifty Thousand only) by way of demand draft in the name of petitioner/wife on the day of hearing/disposal of the petitioner only at the time of hearing of the joint application before the Honble Supreme Court of India or by way of NEFT to the account no. of the petitioner in the bank of Kotak Mahindra Bank, Name  Poonam Kumari, Account No. 7645985808 IFSC No KKBK0000298, Branch-Badshahpur, Gurugram.

H. That both the parties have agreed to withdraw the following/respective cases filed by them against each other and pray the Honble Supreme Court to dispose off the following cases as withdrawn/quashed:

i. Withdrawn the Maintenance case u/s 125 of the CRPC 1973 being MT Case No. 524 of 2023 pending before the Honble Court of Sh. Murray Prasad Singh, Ld. Principal Judge, Family Court, Central District, Tis Hazari, Central Delhi.
ii.

entities.text: Family Court, Central District, Tis Hazari, Central Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Withdraw the Matrimonial (Divorce) Case bearing No. 102024 pending before the Court Sh. Santos Kumar Tiwary, Ld. Principal Judge, Family Court, Madhepura district, Bihar.
iii.

entities.text: Principal Judge, Family Court, Madhepura district, Bihar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Quash the FIR bearing no. 423/2021 dated 7.12.2021 registered at PS Timarpur u/s 406/498A/34 IPC, chargesheet dated 7.8.2023 fled in FIR No. 423/2021 along with all the consequential judicial proceedings which emerged out of the said FIR No.
423/2021.
4. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
The parties would endorse the submissions of the counsel that the disputes between them have been settled in terms of the conditions set out in the settlement agreement.

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the respondent-husband has handed over a demand draft for Rs.12,50,000/- (Rupees Twelve lakhs fifty thousand only) to the petitioner-wife in terms of the settlement agreement.
The receipt of the same is endorsed by the petitioner-wife in Court.

In terms of the settlement clauses A and B of paragraph 6 of the Settlement Agreement, the parties have now filed a joint application under Article 142 of the Constitution of India for dissolution of their marriage by mutual consent.

entities.text: clauses A and B of paragraph 6
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: Going by the other conditions in the Settlement Agreement, in case this application is allowed, the parties have to withdraw their cases filed against each other mentioned in the settlement agreement.

5. After going through the joint application, we are of the considered view that there is no collusion between the parties or threat or influence, in filing the joint application under Article 142 of the Poonam Kumari vs Pranav Kumar on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69687557/
2 Constitution of India to seek for dissolution of marriage.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the parties that the parties are residing separately since 2019.

In the said circumstances, and in view of the fact that their marriage had irretrievably broken down, we are inclined to invoke the power under Article 142 of the Constitution of India and dissolve the marriage between the petitioner and the respondent solemnised on 10.7.2016.
Accordingly, the marriage between the parties stands dissolved.

Consequently, in the following cases filed by the parties stands quashed/disposed of on the following lines:-
i) Matrimonial (Restitution) Case No. 02 of 2021 filed by the respondent-husband,
before Family Court, Madehpura District, Bihar was decreed ex-parte.
The said stands quashed and the Case No. 02/2021 stands disposed of in terms of dissolution of the marriage between the parties.

ii) Complaint filed by the petitioner-wife before the CAW Cell which culminated into FIR NO. 423/2021 under Sections 406, 498A and 34 IPC against the respondent- husband stands quashed and as such the case filed by the respondent-husband bearing Crl. M.C. No.
1122/2024, seeking quashment of FIR No. 423/2021 pending before the High Court of Delhi,
became infructuous.
iii) Maintenance application being MT Case No. 524 of 2023 filed by the Petitioner-wife, pending before the Family Court, Tis Hazari, Central Delhi, stands withdrawn.

entities.text: Family Court, Tis Hazari, Central Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: iv) In view of the order passed in this petition, Matrimonial (Divorce) Case No. 102024 pending before the Family Judge, Madhepura district, Bihar has become infructuous.
6. The Registry shall draw a decree in terms of this order dissolving the marriage of the parties solemnised on 10.7.2016 by mutual consent.
To update the proceedings, the Registry shall also send copies of this order to all the courts concerned where the aforementioned cases are pending to enable updating of their records.
7. Transfer petition and pending application(s), if any, stands disposed of, as above.

,J.
(C.T. RAVIKUMAR) ....................,J.
(PRASHANT KUMAR MISHRA) NEW DELHI;
JULY 15, 2024.
